course: 1C:Enterprise 8 Programming — from foundations to professional development
title: JSON, XML and exchange schemas
goal: Validate JSON/XML schema, types and limits without executing input text.

prerequisites.text: onec.p10; P1–P3; explicit contracts, types, collections and failure handling.

sections.title: Serialization carries data
paragraphs: JSON carries values but does not automatically preserve every 1C-specific type. References need agreed external keys, dates a format/timezone, and money precision rules. A customer display name is not identity. Define required fields, types, ranges and protocol version in a schema.

The complete source accepts JSON text with exactly schemaVersion,minutes,text. Validate string type/4096 length, syntax, field set, types and integer range 0…1440. Parsing alone is not schema validation. This limit applies to materialized input; a network stream needs its own bound.

sections.title: Parsing is not validation
paragraphs: Syntactically valid{"minutes": "30"}can violate a numeric requirement. Do not coerce every input and hide sender defects. Separate parsing, schema validation, business rules and persistence. Handle unknown versions and critical unexpected fields under an explicit policy.

A valid packet uses version 1, numeric 30 and synthetic text containing& and< >. JSON writing/reading preserves number and text. String"30" is deliberately rejected; implicit coercion would change the versioned contract.

sections.title: Bound size and structure
paragraphs: Check byte limits before expensive parsing and structure depth/count during validation. Reject DOCTYPE/ENTITY in teaching XML imports; do not enable external entities for convenience. Never pass text toExecute. Regex is not a general XML parser, so exercise formats are deliberately constrained.

Generate XML only from own data using the platform writer: request root, minutes attribute and text node. The API escapes special characters. This test checks root/attribute and is not a complete arbitrary-XML/XSD validator; it accepts no user DTD/external documents.

sections.title: Test round trips
paragraphs: Serialize a synthetic request, parse and compare semantic fields rather than JSON key order. Include Cyrillic, quotes, zero, missing required data, wrong types and oversized input. Rejection must not leave partially created customers/documents. Raw-payload hash and semantic identity are distinct.

sections.title: Check your explanation
paragraphs: Success is inferred from an unavailable environment. Separate actual observations from a planned advanced scenario and name edition limits.
A failed attempt is removed to make the record look successful. Retain the original failure, its cause, correction and regression evidence.
An own-copy change is applied over the accepted original. Verify the actual directory and preserve source identities before making changes.

practice.task: Investigate the separate adverse case without claiming an unavailable environment was tested. Pass minutes:"30", an unknown field or version 2.
practice.environment: Separate own synthetic infobase; retain the prior module and its backup. Studio and Sandbox optional.

steps.title: Preserve the starting state
steps.action: Close Enterprise. Export a DT backup from Administration → Dump infobase; restore it into a new empty directory and verify the actual path. Preserve earlier functions/fields.
steps.expected: Separate copy opens with the earlier records.
steps.troubleshooting: A new list name alone does not create another database directory.
steps.before: Own path, prior sources and a restorable backup identified.

steps.title: Add the complete server source
steps.action: Create a server/server-call module without Global or Privileged. Paste the complete source below outside other procedures; retain a single shared preparation function if already present.
steps.why: Database access has an explicit server boundary.
steps.expected: Definitions are module-level; no duplicate helper.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not paste definitions inside startup or into an arbitrary Studio file.
steps.before: Separate copy opens with the earlier records.

steps.title: Prepare and call the experiment
steps.why: Print every named result instead of accepting compilation alone.
steps.expected: Only the stated caller is inside the existing startup handler.
steps.troubleshooting: Keep one startup handler; ensure the common module is server-call enabled.
steps.before: Definitions are module-level; no duplicate helper.

steps.title: Save, update and run once
steps.action: Run once and compare the fields with the worked trace. Own root/attribute; Read checked.
steps.why: Observe actual 1C data, not the browser diagram.
steps.troubleshooting: Record the first failed assertion and module/line. Do not change the expectation merely to get True.
steps.before: Only the stated caller is inside the existing startup handler.

steps.title: Retain both results
steps.action: Remove only the startup call. Use another copy for the adverse case and keep both protocols.
steps.why: Preserve provenance and avoid repeating data creation at every startup.
steps.expected: Original retained, negative experiment isolated, automatic caller removed.
steps.troubleshooting: Do not clear registers or delete old documents to make a total agree.
